Quantitative Tissue Phenotyping · Marker explorer

Author and pipeline lead: Yang Cheng · University of Virginia (UVA) · Christopher Deppmann and Melanie Worley laboratories.
Developed with assistance from ChatGPT (OpenAI) in coding, documentation and tutorial preparation.

Choose any three markers. Each point is one nuclear mask. Measurements use raw channel pixels inside that mask.

3D ranges only · Minima stay at zero · Points outside the displayed range are hidden, not removed.

Display contrast does not change measurements or gates. Thresholds are preserved in raw units when the intensity scale changes.

Channel thresholds · all three required

If no file downloads, copy this JSON into a text file with the filename shown above, in Phenotyping_interface. It can be loaded with Import thresholds.

Color = meets all three cutoffs (≥); gray = fails one or more. Cutoffs use the selected intensity scale, and follow each marker within each Plane. Counts include nuclei outside the displayed 3D ranges.

Drag the 3D plot to rotate; hover for cell details. All three 3D axes meet at zero. Marker ranges stay fixed across Planes. Selecting a marker already on another axis swaps the two axes.

Plane inspection · raw channel and nuclear outlines

Select Freehand draw and trace on either image. Release to close the boundary, then name and save. Counts use mask centroids. Overlapping regions count shared masks independently.

Scroll to pan. Both views move together. Auto contrast uses the 1st–99.8th percentiles of this raw channel. Each plane retains its own channel settings.
